comparisons.peer_topic: Accounting Treatment of OCI Reclassifications and Excluded Amounts
comparisons.peer_summary: Amounts reclassified from accumulated OCI are recorded in interest income, market making, compensation, or other income depending on the hedge type; additionally, amounts excluded from effectiveness testing resulted in gains or losses of $252 million, $195 million, and $(38) million in 2024, 2023, and 2022, respectively.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan and Bank of America disclose the reclassification of amounts from Accumulated Other Comprehensive Income (OCI) to earnings, specifically focusing on the impact of hedges. JPMorgan reports a net pre-tax gain of $7 million in 2024, driven by an $89 million gain from net investment hedges offset by an $82 million loss from cumulative translation adjustments. Bank of America discloses that amounts reclassified from accumulated OCI are recorded in interest income, market making, and other income. While JPMorgan provides a consolidated net figure, Bank of America highlights specific gains/losses of $252 million in 2024 resulting from amounts excluded from effectiveness testing, indicating a different granularity in reporting hedge-related reclassifications.

sentences.text: During the year ended December 31, 2024, the Firm reclassified a net pre-tax gain of $7 million to other income/expense, of which $89 million gain related to net investment hedges and $(82) million loss related to cumulative translation adjustments.

Amounts excluded from effectiveness testing and recognized in market making and similar activities were gains (losses) of $252 million, $195 million and $(38) million in 2024, 2023 and 2022, respectively.

comparisons.peer_topic: Net Investment Hedge Gains and Losses in CTA
comparisons.peer_summary: The pretax gain (loss) recorded in the cumulative translation adjustment (CTA) within Accumulated Other Comprehensive Income (AOCI) related to net investment hedges was $2.8 billion, $(1.4) billion, and $370 million for the years ended December 31, 2024, 2023, and 2022, respectively.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies disclose the financial impact of net investment hedges on the Cumulative Translation Adjustment (CTA) within AOCI. JPMorgan reports an $89 million gain related to net investment hedges during 2024 as part of its reclassification activity. Citigroup explicitly quantifies the pretax gain recorded in CTA related to net investment hedges as $2.8 billion for the year ended December 31, 2024. This comparison highlights a significant difference in scale and exposure, with Citigroup reporting a substantially larger pretax gain from its net investment hedging activities compared to JPMorgan.
